title: Count the Number of K-Free Subsets
summary: Given an array of distinct integers and an integer k, count the number of subsets where no two elements have an absolute difference of k.
statement: Given an array of distinct integers and an integer k, count the number of subsets where no two elements have an absolute difference of k. The empty set is considered k-Free. A subset is any selection of elements from the array.
constraints: nums contains distinct integers and k is positive.
A subset is valid when no selected pair has absolute difference exactly k.
Return the number of valid subsets, including the empty subset.
hints: Only values with the same remainder modulo k can differ by exactly k.
Sort each remainder group and use two states: subsets skipping or taking its current value.
If adjacent values differ by k, taking current requires skipping previous; otherwise both previous states may extend either way.
Remainder groups are independent, so multiplying their valid-subset counts forms every global subset exactly once.
editorial: Remainder groups are independent, so multiplying their valid-subset counts forms every global subset exactly once.
